sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay mechanics of Speedy Golf 3D are simple yet challenging. Players use the mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to aim and shoot their golf ball onto the green. The game's controls are easy to learn, but difficult to master, making it a great choice for players of all skill levels. The game's physics engine is also impressive, with realistic ball motion and collision detection that adds to the game's realism.

One of the unique features of Speedy Golf 3D is its three-tap play control. Players can choose from three different control styles: tap, swipe, or hold. The tap control is the most intuitive, requiring players to tap the ball three times to control its trajectory and speed. The swipe control is a bit more challenging, requiring players to swipe the ball in the direction they want it to go. The hold control is the most challenging, requiring players to hold the ball for a certain amount of time before releasing it.

The game's caddy feature is also a nice touch, as it takes care of the math for you, allowing you to focus on your game without worrying about calculating scores. The caddy provides real-time feedback on your shots, including distance, accuracy, and speed. This feature is especially useful for players who are new to golf or want to improve their game quickly.
